meta.purpose: Physical candle wax and wick reference parameters for Delta Hex OS / Math D simulations

waxes.name: Paraffin (Low-Melt / Container)
waxes.burn_behavior: Soft, fast melt pool; high capillary draw; releases heat and vapour readily.

waxes.name: Paraffin (High-Melt / Pillar)
waxes.burn_behavior: Rigid structure; slower melt wall; holds vertical shape without collapsing.

waxes.name: Soy Wax (100% Vegetable)
waxes.burn_behavior: Creamy, slower burn; slightly higher viscosity when liquid than soft paraffin.

waxes.name: Beeswax (Pure)
waxes.burn_behavior: High melt point, dense fuel; burns hot and slow with very low soot/smoke when balanced.

waxes.name: Palm Wax
waxes.burn_behavior: Hard, crystalline structure; melts cleanly into a deep pool once up to temp.

waxes.name: Coconut Wax (Blended)
waxes.burn_behavior: Very low melt point; pools quickly at low heat; usually blended to add rigidity.

waxes.name: Gel Wax (Mineral Oil + Resin)
waxes.burn_behavior: High viscosity and high melt threshold; slow fuel delivery up the wick.

wicks.name: Flat Braid (Cotton)
wicks.behavior: Curls slightly into the flame tip so the end oxidizes cleanly (self-trimming); great for beeswax and pillars.

wicks.name: Square Braid (Cotton)
wicks.behavior: Built for thicker, higher-viscosity waxes like beeswax where steady capillary lift is needed.

wicks.name: Cored Wick (Paper / Cotton Core)
wicks.construction: Braided cotton sleeve around a rigid paper or cotton core
wicks.behavior: Stands straight in deep melt pools; paper cores burn hotter for viscous soy/vegetable waxes.

wicks.name: Cored Wick (Zinc / Tin Core)
wicks.construction: Braided cotton around a thin metal wire core
wicks.behavior: Keeps the wick upright in very hot, deep pools (gels and low-melt container paraffins) without drooping.

wicks.name: Wood Wick (Single / Cross-Ply)
wicks.construction: Thin slotted hardwood strip (cherry, cedar, maple)
wicks.behavior: Wide horizontal flame base; draws fuel across grain channels rather than round threads; emits audible crackle.
